review:
I want to start with this being a VERY good simulator if you just want to fly and race drones, and has a very large focus on being realistic.

However this takes away from the gameplay experience greatly.

The controller compatibility is weird, some parts of the menu are mouse only and some are hard to navigate without controller, plus you practically need a controller for ingame flying.

The freestyle points are calculated weirdly, some gaps feel like they should be counted and some don't, and it's very easy to just spam flips. The coolness factor of watching the replay does not correlate at all to how many points you get.

And the tutorials are incredibly long-winded. The skipping feature is slow and there are these automatic demonstrations that you have to sit and wait through in order to actually try it yourself. 

AND also this is pretty nitpicky but i think the music is a bit repetitive, there are multiple tracks but i hear the same song twice quite often

I am a total novice, and I have never flown a real FPV drone.

I went wild and bought both Liftoff, and Liftoff: Microdrones. I also bought Tryp and Uncrashed.

Out of all of them, Liftoff's maps, UI/UX, and graphics engine were falling short, for me. I also found the racing lines, guides, and flags to be the hardest to read out of all the sims I picked up.

Overall, the most detrimental aspect, for me, is the maps. I think I spoiled myself by starting with Liftoff: Microdrones, and having really intricate and in-depth spaces, then I tried Tryp, which has a lot of details, impressive visual fidelity, and I love being able to enter most buildings/choose time of day/etc.

The new physics are great, and I'm happy that I can still experience them in Liftoff: Microdrones.

There are a lot of FPV sims, and they all have very impressive offerings. Liftoff does bring a wealth of options, utility, customization, and variety to the table. I just think they completely outdid themselves with Liftoff: Microdrones, and I found other comparable titles, to the main Liftoff game, to be a more engaging experience.

I am a complete newbie. I want to learn to fly FPV drones. I watched hours of videos, bought the recommended starter gear and this game. Fired it up, configured the controller. Awesome! Lets do this! 

     1 hr into the sim; Tried the tutorial. "Wow. I suck". Watched more videos. 

     2 hrs into the sim; "Oh that's a controlled altitude and speed straight line! Now let's try some truns....Wow I really do suck!". More videos..... 

     4 hrs into the sim; "I am getting this! Look, nice, clean corners....oh no, I am upside down again."

     8 hrs into the sim; "I think I can do this! At least circles ..... right?" Can't wait any longer! Let's try the real deal!

      Bind all the gear. Charge a couple extra batteries. Set up the drone in the kitchen, lots of room.... right? A couple small hops and .... airborne, right into a wall. Go outside and set up the drone on the deck and off we go! Small controlled flight down into the yard. Landing was rough. "I need more room". Go to the farm. Set everything up and ...... "I am flying ..... I'm f*&king doing it!" 3 batteries, 12 mins of flight and only 2 crash landings on the first 2 landing attempts. Nailed the last landing ... kinda. 

      Get back home, start charging batteries and fire up this amazing simulator. Let's see what another 10, 20, 50+ hours will do to the skills. Highly recommended.

Of the top 5 sims on Steam, this is probably my favorite for a variety of reasons so far. I will say the learning curve is higher than I expected as a fairly experienced RC Pilot with a 107 FAA Certificate. FPV is just a different animal altogether and it is almost a disadvantage to be a mode 2 RC pilot. One thing does still hold true thought pinch the sticks and quit using thumbs only if you want precision control. Also, if you're serious it is worth it to get an actual RC Controller, such as n DJI FPV Remote Controller 3, it makes a ton of difference if you want realistic fpv sim. The options in Liftoff are fantastic and quite complete to dial in whatever you may be after. I still suck at FPV but I am persistent and work on whenever I can catch a moment now that I'm between my favorite RPGs. It
s coming along, but FPV for me isn't a natural gift. More later when I'm able to hold my own in some races ;) Bottom-line, if you on the fence about whether to buy liftoff or not, it's a no-brainer imo, buy it. It'll make you better!
